title: PFCP: Add dissection support for Juniper Filter Variable (32912) and Filter Service Object (32910) IEs
description:
Adds support for dissection of vendor-specific Information Elements (IEs)
32912 (Filter Variable) and 32910 (Filter Service Object) for Juniper
Networks' PFCP extensions.

Both IEs include a length-prefixed byte sequence followed by optionally
printable ASCII data. The dissectors add fields for raw bytes and an
additional string field showing printable ASCII content for improved
readability in the packet tree.

The dissectors use a helper function to suppress non-printable characters
without escaping them as \000 etc., ensuring clean display.

notes.body: do you have look to use FT_STRINGZ ?

The IE data contains embedded nulls and is not null-terminated, so FT_STRINGZ is not suitable - it would stop at the first \0 byte and avoids printing further. Instead, this function extracts and displays only printable characters to avoid \000 type of escape sequences shown by FT_STRING.
So it's the equivalent of what right-clicking on the bytes field and selecting "Copy as ASCII text" would do?
That's right

It doesn't really look like a field of optionally printable ASCII data. It looks like bytes that have some other structure, though within those on occasion there may be ASCII strings or single characters. Ideally it would be further dissected into more fields.

Thanks for the feedback!

You're right, the Filter Variable data isn't structured as a standard ASCII string field. As per the Juniper internal spec (see screenshots), this IE contains opaque binary data with embedded operation flags and sometimes ASCII content. To clarify - the ASCII display is not to imply this is a printable string, it's been added just as a convenience to help developers during debugging like a printable text view for unknown binary data. We are continuing to treat the field as FT_BYTES in the tree, with the ASCII only shown in a separate line for human readability. commits_data.title: PFCP: Add dissection for Juniper Filter Variable and Service Object IEs
commits_data.message:
PFCP: Add dissection for Juniper Filter Variable and Service Object IEs

Adds support for Juniper-specific PFCP IEs 32912 (Filter Variable) and
32910 (Filter Service Object).

Each IE consists of a 2-byte length field followed by a sequence of bytes.
The raw byte field is for each IE is  opaque data which has meaning to the
sending and receiving application.
